title: OpenAI Responses compatibility: seed/determinism flags + metadata passthrough + streaming stability
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers adopting OpenAI's newer Responses API expect parity with Redwood's existing OpenAI-compat endpoints. The Responses API introduces a couple of semantics that our compatibility layer did not fully support: deterministic seeding (seed/determinism flags), richer metadata passthrough on requests/responses, and subtle streaming/event ordering differences for structured outputs and tool/function calling. Motivation: Resolve customer bugs where seed was ignored, metadata fields dropped, and streaming clients saw broken JSON/chunk boundaries when using function calls or structured output. Summary of changes: 1) Add Responses-variant adapter that maps OpenAI Responses fields to Redwood internal request model, including mapping `seed`/`deterministic` to our deterministic_seed pipeline option. 2) Implement metadata passthrough so arbitrary top-level `metadata` on incoming request is forwarded to logs, audit events, and included in proxy responses when the customer requests passthrough, without making it part of model prompt. 3) Streaming stability improvements in the streaming runtime: better backpressure handling, explicit chunk framing for NDJSON structured events, and reassembly logic for function_call payloads to avoid mid-chunk splits that previously produced invalid JSON to clients. 4) Tool/function calling compat: translate OpenAI `function_call` and `tool` invocation fields into Redwood's tool invocation schema and ensure result objects are streamed as structured events. 5) Tests and docs: add unit + integration tests for seed determinism, metadata passthrough, streaming edge-cases; update docs and SDK compatibility shims for Python and TypeScript. Checklist: - [x] Implement adapter mapping for Responses API fields - [x] Map seed/determinism flags to deterministic_seed pipeline option - [x] Preserve request metadata and surface in audit events when passthrough enabled - [x] Improve streaming framing and backpressure tests - [x] Update SDK shims and add examples - [x] Add regression tests and CI coverage - [x] Update docs and changelog Rollout: feature gated behind `openai_responses_compat` feature flag. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compat endpoints. Performance/regressions: local perf tests show <2% median latency impact on streaming requests, peak memory for large tool outputs reduced by 10% due to chunked reassembly. Risk: careful with metadata passthrough to avoid accidental inclusion in prompts; code explicitly keeps `metadata` out of prompt construction. Migration: no user action required other than toggling the feature flag or using the new Responses endpoint. See release notes below for SDK guidance.

review_comments: Miles Chen: Please add a unit test for multiple concurrent streams with interleaved function_call events. Found one edge-case where reassembly would lose last-byte if stream closed aggressively.

release_notes: Adds OpenAI Responses compatibility layer for seed/determinism flags and metadata passthrough. Streaming reliability for structured output and function/tool calling improved. Feature gated behind openai_responses_compat. SDK updates provided for Python/TS.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind feature flag openai_responses_compat. When enabling for customers, monitor streaming error-rate, audit-event size, and deterministic seed experiments. Suggested canary: 1% traffic for 48h then 10% for 72h.
